title: The Wolf and the Crane
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Wolf once got a bone stuck in his throat. So he went to a Crane and begged her to put her long bill down his throat and pull it out. "I'll make it worth your while," he added. The Crane did as she was asked, and got the bone out quite easily.

The Wolf thanked her warmly, and was just turning away, when she cried, "What about that fee of mine?" "Well, what about it?" snapped the Wolf, baring his teeth as he spoke; "you can go about boasting that you once put your head into a Wolf's mouth and didn't get it bitten off. What more do you want?"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what problem does the Wolf have at the start?
options: He has lost his way in the forest
He is trapped in a hunter's snare
A bone is stuck in his throat
He has injured his leg badly

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf ask the Crane to do?
options: Put her long bill down his throat and pull the bone out
Find him something soft to eat instead
Carry a message to another wolf
Warn him if hunters are nearby

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf promise the Crane before she helps him?
options: "I will never bother you again."
"I will protect you from other wolves."
"I will tell everyone of your kindness."
"I'll make it worth your while."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how easily does the Crane remove the bone?
options: Only after several attempts
Quite easily
With great difficulty
Only with the Wolf's help

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Crane ask for once the Wolf turns to leave?
options: A meal in return
An apology for his manners
Her fee
Safe passage home

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf say the Crane should be satisfied with?
options: That she put her head in a Wolf's mouth and wasn't bitten
That she received his warm thanks
That she gained a new friend
That she earned a good reputation among birds

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Wolf's reaction reveal about his earlier promise?
options: He genuinely forgot that he had made a promise at all
He believes the Crane never actually helped him
He is only joking and plans to pay her afterward
He never truly intended to reward the Crane once his own need was met

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why might the Crane have been foolish to trust the Wolf's promise?
options: She did not actually know how to remove the bone properly
She placed herself in a position of danger for a reward that was never guaranteed
She had never dealt with wolves before this encounter
She was tricked into believing the Wolf was a different animal

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "snapped" mean in "snapped the Wolf, baring his teeth"?
options: Whispered gently
Laughed loudly
Spoke sharply and abruptly
Sang cheerfully

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the point of the fable?
options: Doing a dangerous favor for an ungrateful creature may bring no reward beyond having survived it
Cranes should never help wolves under any circumstances
Wolves are always willing to reward those who help them
Removing a bone from a wolf's throat is impossible without injury

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what part of the Crane does the Wolf need to use?
options: Her sharp claws
Her strong wings
Her keen eyesight
Her long bill

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how does the Wolf thank the Crane right after she helps him?
options: He offers her food immediately
He thanks her warmly
He remains silent and walks away
He promises to visit her again soon

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf do with his teeth as he replies to the Crane?
options: He grinds them together
He hides them from view
He bares them
He chatters them nervously

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Wolf frame surviving the encounter as the Crane's true reward?
options: It lets him avoid paying anything while making it sound like she still benefited
He genuinely believes that surviving is the greatest reward of all
He has nothing else of value to offer the Crane
He wants the Crane to feel proud rather than angry

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Wolf's sudden change in tone after the surgery suggest about his character?
options: He genuinely changes his mind out of fairness
He was always hostile, even before asking for help
He becomes friendlier the more he is thanked
He was cooperative only while he needed something from the Crane

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does it mean that the Wolf would "make it worth your while"?
options: He would take a long time to repay her
He would give a reward in exchange for the help
He would ask her to wait patiently
He would apologize for the inconvenience

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: A Crane refuses to help the Wolf and he chokes on the bone
A Wolf and a Crane become close friends after the rescue
A Wolf promises the Crane a reward for helping him, then refuses to pay once the danger has passed
A Crane demands payment before agreeing to help the Wolf
